title: Law 1 holds only while a defn is cold.
problem: Law 1 holds only while a defn is cold. The JIT's int lane keeps intermediates as raw 64-bit words and never wraps them to 63 bits. So once a defn is hot, a comparison or a mod over an add/mul/div that passes 2^62 answers differently from its cold self and from the siblings. kernel-laws-band only checks law 1 cold (bits 1 and 2). Its warm twins cover laws 2 and 6 only, so 5cf407d15's claim that fkwu stands on laws 1-8, and the doc's 'law 1 holds' for fkwu, are wrong for hot code. Hash-shaped recipes are where this bites.
needs: After the op word at fkwu-uni.c:11876, emit `LSL Xd,Xd,#1` (0xD37FF800U|rd<<5|rd) and then `ASR Xd,Xd,#1` (0x9341FC00U|rd<<5|rd). Do the same after the MSUB in kind 15. This is the 63-bit wrap the walker's tagged word gives. Then add a law-1 warm twin bit to kernel-laws-band (the hm shape plus the three lt rows) so the band can fail on it.
evidence: Probe p10: (defn hm (h c) (mod (add (mul h 1099511628211) c) 1000000007)) over 40 inputs i*4000000000123. Cold and after 30000 warm calls disagree on 21 of 40 rows (first row cold 971020198, hot -320151813). Probe p7 at the edge, cold then hot: (lt (add 4611686018427387903 1) 0) gives 1 then 0. (lt (div -4611686018427387904 -1) 0) gives 1 then 0. (lt (mul 3037000500 3037000500) 0) gives 0 then 1. Go answers the cold values. origin/main's runtime/fkwu-uni.c, built in scratch (fkwu-main), gives the same 21/40, so this was already there before the merge.

fixborn.needle: if (!fk_f64_put(words, wn, 0xD37FF800U | ((unsigned int)rd << 5) | (unsigned int)rd)) { return -1; } /* LSL Xd, Xd, #1 */

The walk dirties its own tree: after a turn that ran no gap, the review appends a tracked row that nothing lands. From then on every day turn takes no turn, and so does the night (which only lands afterwards), until a night movement commits hw-paths. When the queue drains, the lane's turns stall for about a cycle, and any gaps added meanwhile wait.

Print `conflict:` only when `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` names a file (otherwise print `dirty:` plus `git status --porcelain`), so hw-conflicted? reads only a real conflict.

title: fcgp-admit is meant to admit a guide's answer only as feedback, never as documents, but it can be bypassed.
problem: fcgp-admit is meant to admit a guide's answer only as feedback, never as documents, but it can be bypassed. It inspects the reply only when the trimmed text starts with '{' and is valid JSON. So documents in a fenced code block, documents wrapped in an array, a capitalised tool name ('Edit') and a plain unified diff are all admitted as feedback text. Band claim 128 tests only a bare object, so it cannot catch this.
needs: Strip ``` fences and parse any JSON object or array found in the reply, checking each element. Compare tool names case-folded and include Edit, Write, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit. Refuse a reply that holds a unified-diff header (a '+++ ' line followed by '@@ '). Add these four shapes to claim 128.
evidence: Probe rv-probe2.bml in a scratch view. A bare {"documents":...} reply: refused guide-carried-documents. The same object in a ```json fence: admitted kind=feedback. Wrapped in an array: admitted. {"tool":"Edit","feedback":...}: admitted. A '--- a/x.fk / +++ b/x.fk / @@' diff: admitted.

answers.text: fcgp-admit now refuses a reply when any JSON value in it carries documents. fcgp-values(t,0,[]) finds every balanced {..} or [..] span that parses, skipping strings and stepping one byte past a span that does not parse. fcgp-node-carries? then walks nested objects and arrays. Tool names are case-folded through str-lower (form-stdlib/string-case.fk) and checked under the keys tool, name and tool_name against edit, write, multiedit, notebookedit and apply_patch. old_string and new_string join the document keys. A '+++ ' line followed by an '@@' line, or '*** Begin Patch', is also refused. A reply that is one fenced feedback object still enters with its text. Claim 128 now has 9 carriers (fenced, array, Edit, MultiEdit tool_use, NotebookEdit in prose, unified diff, nested edits, patch envelope, WRITE) and 4 foils that must still be admitted. Run against the previous code (git show HEAD~4 copy in .hearth/rm-probe2/foil.bml), 7 carriers were admitted and 2 were refused only as guide-answer-empty.

closed_note: fences, arrays, case-folded tool names and unified diffs are refused

title: fccc-heal can overwrite work written after a publish was killed.
problem: fccc-heal can overwrite work written after a publish was killed. The marker records only the pre-publish texts, and heal restores them whenever the marker's pid is dead, without checking that the disk still holds the published candidate. Line 131 promises that a tree that moved since is never overwritten. Publish keeps that promise (fccc-conflict); heal does not. If a killed round leaves a candidate on disk, and Urs, the ladder or a landing then edits or commits that path, the next round's heal silently reverts it. The deferred hook D1 would wire this into the live checkout. fccc-held also publishes when the marker write did not land, because `marked` is never read.

Reviewer probe scratchpad/review-circle/probe-heal.bml, run from the impl worktree root:
- setup: a marker for a dead pid (from /usr/bin/true) with texts ["ORIGINAL\n"], then the source rewritten to "LEGITIMATE LATER EDIT\n", then fccc-heal(root);
- printed 'healed=1' and 'after-heal=ORIGINAL'.
Band claim 256 (marker-heal) only covers the case where the stub still sits on disk, so it cannot catch this.

- fccc-heal-path reads each path. Bytes equal to the checkpoint need nothing. Bytes equal to the ownprint are restored. Any other bytes stay, the marker stays, and the path answers "heal-conflict:<path> holds bytes the killed publish did not write; they stay".
- A marker with no ownprints never overwrites. A marker that cannot be read gives a heal-conflict, never a stop.
- fccc-heal now answers [markers cleared, heal-conflicts]. fccc-circle-rung writes `healed_markers` and `heal_conflicts` into rounds.jsonl, and fccc-healed(r) exposes them.
- New fccc-refused runs before anything is published. It refuses with 'marker-unwritten:' when the marker does not read back as written (fccc-marked? wraps fccc-mark in try). It refuses with 'marker-held:' when this pid already holds a marker.
- Band claims added: 8192 heal-conflict (a later edit stays, the marker stays, the rounds.jsonl row carries the conflict; once the path reads as its checkpoint the next heal clears the marker) and 16384 window-unopened. Claim 256 now heals through the ownprint.

problem:
Unknown cost is recorded as zero, which fl-local-work forbids ('without claiming unknown is zero'):
- A voice that stops is recorded with 0 local IDs. The same goes for the proposer, judge and lesson voice.
- fccc-candidate-of-result reads an absent generated_ids as 0.
The receipt cost and rounds.jsonl local_review_ids then present a lower bound as an exact count. Also, `try X else nothing()` takes the else branch when X answers nothing as well as when it stops. So a voice that answered nothing is logged as 'the voice stopped'.

title: fkwu answers against laws 5-8 where Go, Rust and TS now stand
problem:
Go/Rust/TS meet all four laws on one closure. fkwu (the only runtime) breaks each: float mod is x - y*(double)(long long)(x/y), so it is wrong once |x/y| >= 2^63 and answers x for y = 0.0; float_to_int is ((long long)fk_num(v))<<1 with no check, and fk_num reinterprets a string or nothing word as a huge number; str_to_float is strtod (hex, inf, nan accepted) over the first 126 bytes only, so long strings and long source float literals are silently misread; str_find answers -1 on a non-string. The siblings already answer str_byte_at -1 out of range, so the band comments are stale.
The claim it breaks: docs/kernel-interface.md:55-59 pins: float mod truncates; float_to_int stops on NaN, out-of-range or a non-number; str_to_float reads leading whitespace + longest decimal prefix, no hex, no inf/nan; str_find on a non-string stops. The fkwu str_find comment says the siblings die so no four-way meaning exists; the str-find band says out-of-range str_byte_at is fatal on go/rust/ts.
needs: runtime/fkwu-uni.c: (a) tag 11 float arm: answer NaN when y == 0.0 or x is not finite; answer x when y is infinite or |x| < |y|; otherwise give an exact truncating remainder with the sign of x (libm fmod is exact). (b) tag 54: pass an int through; for a float, fk_stop unless it is finite and -2^62 <= trunc(x) < 2^62; for any other kind, fk_stop('fkwu: float_to_int: only a number reads as an integer -- ask value_kind first'). Make fk_f64_admit refuse t == 54 (return 0 at 10358) until kind 36 carries the same guard. (c) Write one helper, fk_decimal_prefix(sa) -> double. It scans the whole string: ASCII whitespace, an optional sign, digits, an optional '.' and digits, and an optional e/E with a sign and at least one digit. It hands only that prefix to strtod (heap copy when the prefix is longer than 126 bytes) and answers 0.0 when there is no digit. Use it in tags 50, 53 and 113, so the source-literal and intern paths read the same grammar. (d) tag 30: fk_stop when the haystack or needle is not a string. Rewrite the comment at 16052-16055 to the law. form-stdlib/tests/str-find-one-meaning-band.fk: rewrite comments 66-68, 153-157 and 163-165 to today's four-way answers. Then run validate.sh over form-stdlib/tests, since a caller that leaned on str_find(-1) for a nothing haystack now stops.

answers.text: runtime/fkwu-uni.c: float mod is now the exact truncating remainder (new fk_fmod_d). 1e19 mod 3 is 1, 1e300 mod 3 is 0, a zero divisor or infinite dividend gives NaN. Tag 54 float_to_int passes an int through, truncates a float in [-2^62, 2^62), and stops on NaN, out-of-range values and other kinds. The JIT kind-36 leaf now does FCMP plus B.VS and a 63-bit round-trip CMP plus B.NE to the overflow block, so the walker answers and stops. One reader, fk_decimal_prefix, scans the whole text with no 126-byte cap; tags 53, 50 and 113 all use it, so a 131-digit text or source literal reads its own value and 0x10, inf and nan read 0. Tag 30 str_find stops on a non-string haystack or needle (comment rewritten to the law). Stale comments in str-find-one-meaning-band.fk rewritten to today's four-way answers. Docs F3 is the same gap and is closed by this.

title: fkwu math_exp, math_log and math_pow never return on infinities and huge inputs, answer 0 for log(<=0), read non-numbers
problem:
fk_exp_d computes n=(long long)(x/ln2) and loops r -= ln2 and sum *= 2 n times: exp(+-inf) and exp(1e300) loop forever, exp(1e9) takes 3.3 s. fk_log_d halves x while x >= 2.0, so log(+inf) loops forever; it answers 0.0 for any x <= 0. fk_pow_d casts an infinite or >= 2^63 exponent to long long and calls fk_exp_d on the remainder, so pow(2, inf) loops forever. Non-numbers are read through fk_num and answer numbers. Results are 1-3 ulp off the siblings.
The claim it breaks: Host and core doors answer a value or stop; no door ends or wedges the process (kernel-interface.md:90-94). primitive-registry.fk:406-408 lists math_pow/log/exp as four-way natives.
needs: runtime/fkwu-uni.c, as the finder proposes. fk_exp_d: guard NaN, x > 709.79 and x < -745.14 first, then scale by 2^n built from exponent bits instead of loops. fk_log_d: NaN or x < 0 -> NaN, 0 -> -inf, +inf -> +inf, then take the exponent and mantissa from the bits. fk_pow_d: handle the IEEE special cases for an infinite y and |y| >= 2^53 before any (long long) cast. Arms 81/89/90/195: call fk_arith_check (or stop) on a non-number before fk_num, which also ends the math_exp(nothing) spin. If bit agreement is wanted, linking libm exp/log/pow is the smallest path: all three siblings agree to the bit on every row above.
evidence:
cd cut10x; for each expression print -r -- "(do (print (value_str E)) 0)" > $S/hang.fk; $S/bounded.sh 5 ./fkwu $S/hang.fk: (math_log (div 1.0 0.0)), (math_exp (div 1.0 0.0)), (math_exp (div -1.0 0.0)), (math_pow 2.0 (div 1.0 0.0)), (math_exp 1e300) each '@bounded: killed after 5s'. /usr/bin/time -p on (math_exp 1000000000.0): '=> Infinity real 3.32'; (math_exp -1000000000.0) real 4.21. $S/math.fk four-way: 'log 0' fkwu 0 vs -Infinity on Go/Rust/TS; 'log -1' 0 vs NaN; 'log str' 0 vs stop ('AsFloat: x'); 'sqrt str' NaN vs stop; 'exp 1' 2.7182818284590446 vs 2.718281828459045; 'pow 2 0.5' 1.4142135623730954 vs 1.4142135623730951. My first unbounded four-way run hung at 'log inf' (task moved to background after 120 s).
Verified confirmed: cd cut10x; each expression written as (do (print (value_str E)) 0) and run with $V/bounded.sh 4 ./fkwu: (math_log (div 1.0 0.0)), (math_exp (div 1.0 0.0)), (math_pow 2.0 (div 1.0 0.0)) and (math_exp 1e300) each '@bounded: killed after 4s'. One more the finder did not show: (math_exp (nothing)) gives '@bounded: killed after 5s'. fk_num reads nothing as about -4.5e18, so fk_exp_d runs its n loop for about 6.5e18 steps. My unbounded run of it had to be killed by its pid. Same expressions on Go, Rust and TS: [Infinity, Infinity, 0, Infinity, Infinity]. $V/v2b.fk on fkwu: [0, 0, 0, NaN, 2.7182818284590446, 1.4142135623730954, 2.3025850929940455] for log 0, log -1, log "x", sqrt "x", exp 1, pow 2 0.5, log 10. All three siblings: [-Infinity, NaN, null(stop 'AsFloat: x'), null(stop), 2.718281828459045, 1.4142135623730951, 2.302585092994046]. title: write_file_bytes truncates a file and reports success when handed a string; byte lists are written unchecked
problem:
The sibling door write_file_bytes (fkwu mode 27) still opens with O_TRUNC before looking at its argument: a string or int empties the existing file and answers 0. Go does the same, and Go's file_append_bytes still answers the file size for a string, int or nothing while writing nothing (the exact defect healed in fkwu). fk_write_byte_list (used by both fkwu doors) and Go's byte(v.Int) write any element as a byte: 300 becomes 44, -1 becomes 255, a string becomes the low byte of its word. Rust stops and TS answers -1 in every one of these cases.
The claim it breaks: Today's commit bb6eb12b5 healed file_append_bytes on fkwu: 'a string or any other kind is refused like a failed open, never answered as a complete write of nothing'. A door answers its value or a refusal.
needs: Use one refusal, -1, the door's stated '| -1'. fkwu: hoist the tag-61 predicate at 16497 into a helper fk_is_list_word(x), call it in mode 27 BEFORE open(O_TRUNC), and pre-scan the list so that a non-int element refuses before any byte is written (the int &0xff masking stays: it is four-way). Go main.go:2670-2705: both natives answer -1 before os.WriteFile/OpenFile unless args[1].Kind == VList and every element is a VInt. Rust main.rs:4254: answer Value::Int(-1) instead of Null, and refuse a non-int element instead of panicking in as_int. A refused write leaves the old bytes standing.
evidence:
printf 'precious' > $S/keep.txt; (write_file_bytes "$S/keep.txt" "hello"): fkwu 'answer => 0' and wc -c reads 0; Go (re-seeded) 'answer => 0', size 0. $S/wfb.fk four-way: fkwu str 0, int 0, bad list (list 300 "x" -1) 3 (3 bytes written, od ', 366 377'); Go str 0, int 0, nothing 0, bad list 3; Rust: all four stop, no file created; TS: -1 for each, no file. $S/append.fk: Go 'str => 5', 'int => 7', 'nothing => 7' (size unchanged, success); fkwu 'list w 300 => 5' (3 garbage bytes appended); Rust stop 'as_int: Str'; TS -1. fkwu-uni.c:15329 'tmp[n] = (char)(FK_HH(q) >> 1);' with no kind or range check; Go main.go:2673 'bytes[i] = byte(v.Int)'.
Verified partial: Holds: each file pre-seeded with 'precious' (8 bytes), then $V/v4.fk. (write_file_bytes p "hello") answers 0 on fkwu and Go and the file shrinks to 0 bytes; (write_file_bytes p 7) does the same. Go (file_append_bytes p "hello") answers 8 (the unchanged size, reported as success); fkwu answers -1. A string element inside the list (list 300 "x" -1): fkwu writes bytes 44,248,255 (the string word's low byte) and Go writes 44,0,255, while Rust stops ('as_int: Str') and TS answers -1. Code read: fkwu-uni.c:15426-15437 opens with O_TRUNC before any kind check (the guard at 16497 exists only on tag 61); Go main.go:2671-2675 does byte(v.Int) over args[1].List with no kind check. REFUTED part: 'Rust stops and TS answers -1 in every one of these cases' is wrong for an out-of-range int. $V/v4b.fk (list 119 300 -1) through both doors writes bytes 119 44 255 and answers 4/3 on ALL FOUR kernels. TS kernel.ts:1515-1516 documents it ('Values out of 0..255 truncate per Go's byte(v.Int) and Rust's as u8'), and Rust uses 'as_int() as u8' at main.rs:4253,4268. The masking is one agreed meaning, not a fkwu/Go defect. One more split: on a non-list, Rust write_file_bytes answers nothing (main.rs:4254 'return Value::Null') and TS answers -1, so the refusal has three spellings.

answers.text: fkwu part: fk_byte_list_ok (a list whose every element is an int) is checked before open in mode 27 write_file_bytes and in tag 61 file_append_bytes. A string, a number, nothing or a list holding a non-int now gives -1, and the existing bytes are left as they were. Masking an out-of-range int to its low byte is unchanged; all four kernels share that.

Go main.go:2670-2705: write_file_bytes and file_append_bytes return -1 before os.WriteFile/OpenFile unless args[1].Kind == VList and every element is VInt (keep byte(v.Int)). Rust main.rs:4254: Value::Int(-1) instead of Null for a non-list, and -1 instead of an as_int panic for a non-int element.

title: Both queued gaps carry an rg -c check that the lane's own rg tool can never satisfy
problem:
The native rg prints the path in count mode for every search (far-doc-output: path + ":" + n + "\n"), and far-format does the same in lines mode. So the check refuses every candidate. Real ripgrep 15.2.0 prints only the count for a single file. Option 1's final unpublished candidate passes the balance and arity checks and reads 31 (full) under the band's body; only the rg check refuses it. The lane spent options 1 and 2 (113 min, 48 turns) and option 3 (still running at 16:43) on a gap it had already solved.
The claim it breaks: The queue rows check with ripgrep's single-file shape: {"tool":"rg","arguments":["-c","-F","(defn cl-unit-at","form/form-stdlib/closure-lines.fk"],"stdout":"1\n"}. sort-home uses the same shape for "(defn sort-by". The lane's checks are meant to be passable by a correct candidate.
needs: Change only the queue. In learn/native-turn-queue.jsonl, row 1's check stdout becomes "form/form-stdlib/closure-lines.fk:1\n" and row 2's becomes "form/form-stdlib/sort.fk:1\n". These match the native tool's documented shape. The probe shows exactly those bytes, with exit 0 and empty stderr, which fcaq-tool-matches accepts. Do not change rg to ripgrep's filename rule: that breaks docs/form-native-agent-tools.md:260 and every caller that relies on the prefix. A form-agent-search band stays worth adding, but it is separate work. The finder's claim that the candidate already under .hearth would publish green is not verified: changing checks changes the checkpoint key (fcam-prepare is keyed on json-emit(checks), form-cli-code-request.bml:119).
evidence:
Probe scratch/rg-count-probe.bml calls fat-call(docs,"rg",["-c","-F","(defn cl-unit-at",path],"") on a one-document corpus containing the defn and prints: exit=0 stdout=[form/form-stdlib/closure-lines.fk:1
] matches-check-stdout=0. Real ripgrep: `rg -c -F '(do' form/form-stdlib/sort.fk` gives `1`, `rg -n -F '(do' sort.fk` gives `6:(do`, and only two files or -H add the path. Probe scratch/checks-probe.bml runs the three request checks over option 1's result documents[0]: rg holds=0 (actual "form/form-stdlib/closure-lines.fk:1
"), balance holds=1, arity holds=1. Probe scratch/clb-candidate-band.fk is the band body with the candidate's four defns inlined; ./fkwu prints 31. Option 1 retains 4 rg failures in its repair notes and option 2 retains 8, all with the path-prefixed actual (command grep -a counts on the result lines). No band exercises fat-call or far-run: grep of form/form-stdlib/tests, observe/tests and gate for form-agent-(tools|search) finds nothing.
Verified confirmed: Probe verify-lane/rg-shape.bml (./fkwu from cut10x root): `one-c exit=0 stdout="form/form-stdlib/closure-lines.fk:1
"`, `one-c-equals-queue-stdout=0`, `one-n stdout="form/form-stdlib/closure-lines.fk:1:(do
"`, `two-c stdout="a.fk:1
b.fk:1
"`, and `-H`/`-I` both `exit=2 error="unsupported-rg-option"`. Real ripgrep 15.2.0: `rg -c -F '(do' form/form-stdlib/sort.fk` prints `1`. form-cli-code-request.bml:85 (fcaq-tool-matches) compares stdout bytes exactly. One correction: the native rg follows its own written contract. docs/form-native-agent-tools.md:260 says "Search output always carries its source path, even for one document." title: The band never reads an unpublished candidate, so the walk cannot tell a check no candidate can pass from a lane that failed
problem:
nt-publishable needs status complete with release_ok 1, and the band runs only when published > 0 (after = published > 0 ? nt-band(...) : before). A candidate that a wrong check refused is therefore never measured. The repair note at attempt 6 (check run 1, turn 8) records the candidate refused on the rg row alone. The walk then resumed it for 2 more options while the row recorded band_after null. Nothing proves a gap's checks pass on its reference: no gate or door reads learn/native-turn-queue.jsonl except the turn, the review and host-walk.
The claim it breaks: Offer (docs:196) says a gap is 'a band proven reachable by a reference solution held outside the tree, total over any candidate'. The walk is described as a backtrack walk that learns from what each option saw.
needs: In nt-attempt, when the lane returns writable documents but is not ready and there is no conflict: publish them with nt-publish, run nt-band within its 10-minute deadline, then call nt-keep. nt-keep already writes <stamp>-<base>.candidate and restores the originals, which also heals the header's keep claim. Write candidate_band (a number or null) into the row. When candidate_band == full, nt-option returns oac-nothing, and the finding names the lane's last refusing check, taken from the last repair_notes evidence. That gap's contract is unwinnable, and the lane is not at fault. In docs/form-native-coding.md, the Offer step adds: 'and its checks pass on that same reference through the lane's own native tools (fat-call)'.
evidence:
Walk ledger rows for closure-unit-line options 1 and 2: published 0, band_before null, band_after null, lane_status attention, wall 4768818 and 2016123 ms. The band-body probe of option 1's candidate prints 31. The checks probe shows balance and arity hold. command grep -a -rn 'native-turn-queue' gate/ validate.sh docs finds only docs/form-native-coding.md:195.
Verified confirmed: observe/native-turn-run.bml:167: nt-publishable needs status complete and release_ok 1. Line 225 publishes only when ready, and line 226 reads `let after = published > 0 ? nt-band(band,full) : before;`. Walk ledger (/Users/ursmuff/source/coherence-kernel-walk/receipts/native-turn-ledger.jsonl), closure-unit-line options 1 and 2: `"band_before":null,"band_after":null`, `"published":0`, `"lane_status":"attention"`, wall_ms 4768818 and 2016123. Option 1's candidate reads 31 in the band body (clb-cand.fk). Option 1's repair notes 6-9 show the rg row as the only refusal. docs/form-native-coding.md:195-197 says the Offer step needs "a band proven reachable by a reference solution held outside the tree", but nothing checks that the gap's checks pass on that reference. Line 232 (`kept = if published == 0 ... then 0`) also means an unpublished candidate is never written as a .candidate file: ls of the walk's .hearth/native-turns shows no closure-unit-line-*.candidate. That contradicts the header at lines 9-11, which says a non-green option "keeps its candidate under .hearth/native-turns".

title: Each resumed option is told its code did not compile (stale before-band errors), and the lane's own failing check is left out
problem:
When published == 0, after = before (nothing), so errors = nt-band-errors() reads .hearth/native-turns/band.err from the run before the lane, and nt-band-claims reads the same stale file. The feedback says "The band did not read; the compiler said: ... 'cl-unit-at' matched no op" about a candidate that defines cl-unit-at and reads 31. The real blocker, the rg check's actual output, never appears. Each later option gets the same text with only the attempt number changed.
The claim it breaks: An option that did not turn green 'acks a node carrying what it saw (the band's reading, the lane's status, the candidate's diff, and the compiler's own words when the band did not read)'. Later options resume 'with that finding'.
needs: In nt-attempt (native-turn-run.bml:227 and :230), compute errors and claims only when this option ran the band (published > 0). Otherwise the finding says 'the band was not run on this option: nothing was published'. It adds the lane's last repair note evidence (result repair_notes[-1].evidence, trimmed to about 600 bytes) beside the reason. Each resumed option then hears the failing check and its actual.
evidence:
diff of the feedback field in .hearth/native-turns/closure-unit-line-1790839622339.json (option 2) and -1790841638464.json (option 3): the only difference is 'Attempt 1' vs 'Attempt 2' and the id; diff-rc=1 with one changed line. Both carry five 'closure-lines-band.fk:NN: error: [unresolved-call] cl-unit-at' lines and 'Coding observation: caller-turn-budget-reached;checkpoint-retained'.
Verified confirmed: native-turn-run.bml:226-227: when published == 0, after = before (nothing), so errors = nt-band-errors() reads band.err from the run at turn start. I extracted the feedback field from walk .hearth/native-turns/closure-unit-line-1790839622339.json and -1790841638464.json and diffed them: one changed line, 'Attempt 1' against 'Attempt 2' plus the id. Both carry five `closure-lines-band.fk:NN: error: [unresolved-call] 'cl-unit-at'` lines, then 'Coding observation: caller-turn-budget-reached;checkpoint-retained'. title: The queue's full is a second copy of the band's Verdict pin, and a band reading above full is treated as open forever
problem:
nt-turn compares the reading with the queue row's full only. When the band gained a claim (pin 3 to 7) and the queue kept full 3, every option was asked to bring a band reading 7 down to 3. That cannot be done without breaking a claim. The lane spent 8 options on main's ledger (10 in the walk) on it.
The claim it breaks: A band's head pin is its '; Verdict n' line. nt-turn closes a gap when its band reads full.
needs: Add nt-pin(band), which reads the '; Verdict <n>' head line from the band file. observe/band-pin-run.bml already parses the same head. nt-turn takes full from the pin. When the queue's full is present and differs, the turn does not walk: it appends a row with contract_moved {queue_full, pin} and prints '[native-turn] <id> contract moved'.
evidence:
In main's receipts/native-turn-ledger.jsonl, command grep -a -c '"band_before":7,"band_after":7,"full":3' gives 8, with wall_ms 1678274+925587+1505708+766145+1025223+691906+778573+752528 (about 135 min). `git show c134b04bb:learn/native-turn-queue.jsonl` gives full 3 for bml-cursor-reads-sections. `git show c134b04bb:form/form-stdlib/tests/form-bml-cursor-reader-band.bml` gives '; Verdict 3'. Verified confirmed: native-turn-run.bml:179 reads full from the queue row, and :183 and :228 compare against it alone. In main's receipts/native-turn-ledger.jsonl, `command grep -a -c '"band_before":7,"band_after":7,"full":3'` gives 8, all for gap bml-cursor-reads-sections. Their wall_ms values sum to 8123944 (135.4 min). `git show c134b04bb:learn/native-turn-queue.jsonl` gives `"full":3,"id":"bml-cursor-reads-sections"`. The c134b04bb band reads '; Verdict 3', and today's reads '; Verdict 7 = 1 runs | 2 refuses | 4 collections'. The defect is latent today: both queue rows hold full 31, and closure-lines-band.fk:3 and sort-band.fk:3 both read '; Verdict 31'. The code still holds the second copy.

title: The day-turn window limits when turns start, not how long they run: one turn is a walk of up to six options with no wall deadline
problem:
dt-land checks the window only after a turn has landed. hw-native-turn passes only {"turns":24}, and nt-local-attempts defaults to 6 options. Measured option walls are 79.5, 33.6 and more than 42 min, so one turn can run 4 to 8 hours. hw-native-turn also greps '[native-turn] ' | tail -1, so the walk's verdict line ('[native-turn:walk] ... declined after N option(s)') never reaches the day-turn or night log.
The claim it breaks: day-turn.bml:6 says the window is 'two and a half hours, so the 12:30 and 19:00 slots never meet the next'.
needs: hw-native-turn(turns, until) passes {"turns":24,"until_unix_ms":until}. Use the wall clock: the child can read it, and monotonic across processes is unverified. nt-option returns oac-nothing once now_unix_ms() > until, and the walk line says 'window-ended'. hw-native-turn greps -F '[native-turn' so it keeps both the last row and the walk line. day-turn passes its window end and scheduled-walk passes 05:30. dt-run skips turns when sync is not sync=0.
evidence:
ps: ./fkwu observe/day-turn.bml pid 14693 started 14:05:54 (its window ends 16:35:54). native-turn-run pid 20244 started at 14:07:12, and its options were stamped 14:07:33, 15:27:02 and 16:00:38. At 16:39:54 option 3 (form-cli-code-run pid 89723) was at turn 56 and still running. git show 43ffe584f:observe/day-turn.bml shows the dt-window-ms loop is in the code that is running. All day-turn.log runs before 14:02 used the one-turn version (the loop arrived in 743e0f7b4).
Verified confirmed: day-turn.bml:26-35: dt-turns runs hw-native-turn(24), and dt-land checks `host_monotonic_ms() < until` only after a landing. host-walk.bml:22 passes only {"turns":24} and greps -F '[native-turn] ' | tail -1, so the walk line '[native-turn:walk] ...' never matches. native-turn-run.bml:185 defaults to 6 options, and the probe len(0 .. 6)=6 confirms the count. ps at 16:49:32: 14693 `./fkwu observe/day-turn.bml` started 14:05:54 (its window ended 16:35:54); 20244 native-turn-run started 14:07:12; 89723 form-cli-code-run started 16:00:38, at turn 57 at 16:54. Option request mtimes: 14:07, 15:27, 16:00. `git show 43ffe584f:observe/day-turn.bml` (the walk's HEAD) has the dt-window-ms loop, which arrived in 743e0f7b4 at 14:02:02. Also read: no single-run guard exists (command grep for lock, host_alive or pgrep in day-turn.bml, host-walk.bml and scheduled-walk.bml finds only nt-band-wait). dt-run (day-turn.bml:39-43) runs turns whatever hw-sync answered. The plist's 19:00 slot uses the same WorkingDirectory, so a session-begun turn with no deadline can meet the next slot in one checkout.

answers.text: Each turn now gets its wall deadline. hw-native-turn(turns, deadline) in form/form-stdlib/bml/host-walk.bml sends {"turns":24,"deadline_ms":<the window's end on host_monotonic_ms>} on stdin to observe/native-turn-run.bml. The day turn's window is its start + 9000000 ms (12:30-15:00, 19:00-21:30). The night's window is its start + 7200000 ms (03:30-05:30).

title: The review's 'speed' is generated IDs over whole option wall. It is not generation speed, cannot clear on this host, and no phase cost reaches a ledger
problem:
The rate is the sum of generated IDs over the sum of whole-option wall_ms. That wall includes compile, seal, prefill, observation injection, context renewal and tools. Folding the lane's own form-code progress lines gives decode at only 64.6% and 61.4% of the wall. The threshold of 4 IDs/s is above this host's decode itself (1.74 and 3.42 IDs/s), so 'speed' can never clear. The rows carry no phase split and no contention reading, while back-to-back options of one gap differ 2x in decode and 4x in prefill.
The claim it breaks: The review prints 'local generation runs X IDs/s', and Urs's direction (form-lift fl-local-work) asks to 'observe context, release, and live phase costs'.
needs: No change to the lane files is needed: the lane already prints 'form-code {...elapsed_ms, generated_ids, injected_ids...}' to outPath. nt-attempt folds those lines (deltas, as pf.bml does) into decode_ms, inject_ms, host_ms and first_token_ms on the row. The review computes decode IDs/s as generated over decode_ms, names the largest phase in its speed line, and compares with the host's own earlier decode readings instead of a fixed 4/s.

Probe scratch/phase-fold.bml folds the deltas between consecutive form-code lines. Option 1 (wall 4768.8 s): 87.5 s spawn and compile (re-lowering form-cli-code-run.fk), 65.1 s seal, 15.4 s prompt cursor, 28.5 s model open, 224.4 s initial prefill of 2497 IDs (11.1 IDs/s), decode 3079.1 s over 5343 IDs (576 ms/ID), injection 1023.3 s over 13513 IDs (13/s), context renewal 214.9 s (re-prefill of 4208 IDs at remaining_positions 53 of 16384), tools and checks about 29 s, tail 0.7 s. Option 2 (2016.1 s): seal 14.2 s, prefill of 4905 IDs in 106.1 s (46/s), decode 1238.4 s (292 ms/ID), injection 534.4 s (20/s), renewal 87.0 s. The band runs once per walk (about 21 s, 14:07:12 to 14:07:33) and never after an option. A scratch replay of the review over a copy of the walk's ledgers (scratch/walkview) prints 'next: speed — local generation runs 1.4 IDs/s across lane wall time'. Decode-only over both options is 9580/4317.5 s = 2.22 IDs/s.
Verified confirmed: local-flow-review.bml:84-85: rate = sum generated / sum wall_ms over rows. :62 fires 'speed' below 4000 milli-IDs/s, ahead of queue and turn. Walk rows give 9580/6784941 ms = 1.41 IDs/s. I reran the phase fold (verify-lane/pf.bml, a copy of the finder's) on the lane's own progress lines. Option 1: decode-ms=3079057 over generated=5343 (576 ms/ID, 1.74 IDs/s), inject-ms=1023328 over 13513, host-ms=244215, first-elapsed-ms=334634. Option 2: decode-ms=1238423 over 4237 (292 ms/ID, 3.42 IDs/s), inject-ms=534430 over 10878, first-elapsed-ms=145739. Decode is 64.6% and 61.4% of wall, and even decode-only stays under 4/s, so 'speed' cannot clear on this host. Option 1's .out.err shows `observe/form-cli-code-run.fk.fkb: bml cache does not match today's bytes; re-lowering`, about 84.6 s, then the seal from 1790834940972 to 1790835006069 (65.1 s). Rows carry no phase field (row shape at native-turn-run.bml:233-234). HEAD a0c5c01e5 changed only the speed text.

title: The local share counts only voice drafts: coding-lane IDs a session started never reach its row
problem:
sr-local reads only receipts/draft-ledger.jsonl. A native-turn row names its coordinator by exe path (the claude binary), not by session, so the lane's generated IDs cannot be joined to the session that began the turn. host_process already answers argv, so the session id is readable from the coordinator's --resume= argument.
The claim it breaks: The session-rent row puts the session's rented tokens 'beside the local tokens that served it'. The local_share_ppm is the walk's measure.
needs: nt-coordinator also returns the session id from the climbed row's argv (row[4]: '--resume=<id>' or '--session-id' <id>), and the row writes "session". sr-local also sums local_generated_ids from native-turn-ledger rows with that session, reported as lane_generated beside drafts, and the share includes it.
evidence:
receipts/session-rent-ledger.jsonl for session 39d16a37: local drafts 6, generated 2239, local_share_ppm 535 (output 4180671). ps -o command for pid 14691 (parent of day-turn 14693) shows zsh running `S=.../39d16a37-.../scratchpad; cd /Users/ursmuff/source/coherence-kernel-walk && ./fkwu observe/day-turn.bml`, and its parent 47959 is claude --resume=39d16a37-d4e8-4631-9ac0-105916d511fd. The walk rows from that turn read coordinated_by session and rented_mind 1, with local_generated_ids 5343 and 4237. Counting them gives (2239+9580)*1e6/(11819+4180671) = 2819 ppm. Probe scratch/proc-probe.bml shows host_process(pid) = [pid, ppid, exe, cwd, [argv...], start_ms, 0].
Verified confirmed: session-rent.bml:50-56: sr-local reads only the draft ledger rows that carry "session":"<id>". native-turn-run.bml:122 records only the exe path (nt-exe). In main's receipts/session-rent-ledger.jsonl, the session 39d16a37 row shows `"local":{"drafts":6,"generated":2239},"local_share_ppm":535`, output 4180671. ps shows coordinator 47959's argv holding `--resume=39d16a37-d4e8-4631-9ac0-105916d511fd`. Probe verify-lane/pv.bml reads host_process(47959) and prints `len=7 exe-tail=claude argv-n=30 resume-at=12`, so row[4] is argv. The walk rows read coordinated_by session, with local_generated_ids 5343 and 4237. Counting them: (2239+9580)*1e6/(11819+4180671) = 2819 ppm.

answers.text: session-rent.bml: sr-lane sums the local_generated/injected_ids of native-turn rows carrying "session":<id>, read where turns run (sr-turn-rows). The row gains local.lane_options, lane_generated and lane_injected, and local_share_ppm counts lane generated IDs. The writer half (native-turn-run.bml writing "session") is deferred, so today no row carries it and lane share reads 0 for every session.

In observe/native-turn-run.bml add, after nt-coordinator (:122): `def nt-session-arg(argv, prev) = if nil?(argv) then "" else if nt-starts?(argv[0], "--resume=") then substring(argv[0], 9, len(argv[0])) else if (((String) prev == "--resume") || ((String) prev == "--session-id")) then argv[0] else nt-session-arg(argv[1:], argv[0]);` `def nt-session() { let row = nt-climb(nt-parent(nt-self()), 8); if (len(row) < 5) then "" else nt-session-arg(row[4], ""); }`. Then in nt-attempt's row (:233) add `fhn-s("session", nt-session())`. host_process row[4] is argv, per the survey's probe.

title: The turn meter and flow meter read only the main transcript; session-rent alone reads subagents, so the same session reads about 40% apart
problem:
All four meters agree exactly on the main transcript. The turn meter and flow meter never open <session>/subagents/*.jsonl, so an asking that fans out to subagents looks cheap, and a movement's flow row undercounts its rented spend.
The claim it breaks: Each meter has one job: the turn meter answers 'which asking inside a Claude transcript was expensive' and the flow meter answers 'a movement's calls'. Session-rent reads the transcript 'and every subagent transcript beside it'.
needs: Both meters read sr-files(main) the way session-rent does. Each subagent transcript is credited to the turn whose window holds its first timestamp, deduped by request id across files. The flow row adds subagent_requests and subagent_output.
evidence:
Probe scratch/meters4.bml over transcript .../jovial-aryabhata-3751d7/6f04f4fa-....jsonl with no ledger write. Session-rent main-only: requests 561, cache_write 5157565, cache_read 232257380, output 708814. Session-rent with 28 subagent files: requests 2979, cache_write 13370964, cache_read 561097482, output 993364. Turn meter: 67 turns, 561 messages, output 708814. Flow meter: provider_turns 561 (provider_calls 1246), output 708814. Rented-turn-meter: 708814.
Verified partial: Rerunning the finder's probe (verify-lane/m4.bml) over .../jovial-aryabhata-3751d7/6f04f4fa-e38b-4ff6-a987-23bcca1ccece.jsonl reproduces exactly. session-rent main-only: requests=561, output=708814. With 28 subagent files: requests=2979, output=993364 (+40%). Turn meter: turns=67, messages=561, output=708814. Flow meter: provider_turns=561, provider_calls=1246, output=708814. Rented-turn-meter: 708814. In code, form-cli-turn-meter.bml:73 and form-cli-flow-meter.bml:103 each read one path. This is not a mirrorlag, though. docs/form-native-coding.md:229-238 scopes the turn meter to 'which asking inside a Claude transcript' and claims subagents only for session-rent. Nothing says the turn and flow meters read subagents, so this is a dark spot (an asking that fans out reads cheap), and it sits off the lane face.

answers.text: I made the meters agree rather than fold them; each keeps one job. form-cli-turn-meter.bml and form-cli-flow-meter.bml now read sr-files (main transcript plus subagent transcripts, depth first), deduped per message/request id. The turn meter credits each subagent transcript to the asking whose timestamp is at or before its first timestamp and shows subagent_messages, subagent_output and subagent_transcripts per turn. The flow row adds transcripts, subagent_provider_turns and subagent_output_tokens. Real session 6f04f4fa now reads the same three ways: 2979 requests, 993364 output, 575470964 total (turn and flow read 708814 before). rented-turn-meter-run.fk keeps its one-transcript count and prints subagent-transcripts=28 beside it. I also removed its doubled newlines, and turn-meter-run's (no consumers parse them; grep confirmed).

title: The review on main reads none of the lane's local IDs: rows reach main only through a landing, and a landing that fails on a network error is not retried
problem:
Turns run in the walk checkout. Their rows reach main only when the turn's whole walk lands, which can be hours later. hw-carry's fast-forward repairs only a moved main ('fetch first', 'non-fast-forward', 'rejected'), so a DNS failure holds the landing until the next walk. Main's review today read 0 generated IDs while the walk held 9580 IDs and 113 min of lane wall.
The claim it breaks: The review opens every session with the local flow ('local tokens should be higher'), reading both ledgers.
needs: (1) In hw-carry's fast-forward, add live-repair('wait for the network', words 'Could not resolve host'|'unable to access', host_sleep_ms 60000 then hw-follow), at most twice. (2) local-flow-review also reads the walk checkout's ledger (WorkingDirectory from docs/launchd/earth.hati.day-turn.plist), dedupes by at_unix_ms+gap+option, and names each count's checkout. This shares host-walk.bml with F6 and local-flow-review.bml with F7 and F11.

Could not resolve host: github.com' and 'main=128 held'. `git branch -r --contains 43ffe584f` gives only origin/claude/form-cli-direct-guided-01ya6p. Diffing at_unix_ms between main's and the walk's ledgers: main lacks 1790831077935, 1790832493923 (committed, stranded), 1790839622336 and 1790841638463 (uncommitted, running turn). command grep -a -c local_generated_ids on main's ledger gives 0. main's receipts/local-flow-review.jsonl has 3 rows today, all local_generated_ids 0 and next 'turn'.
Verified confirmed: day-turn.log (120 lines), lines 118-119: `[carry] sync=0 ahead=1 drift-gates pass=31 full=31 refused=0 names=- fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/seeker71/coherence-kernel.git/': Could not resolve host: github.com` and `main=128 held`. host-walk.bml:58 repairs only 'fetch first', 'non-fast-forward' and 'rejected'. `git branch -r --contains 43ffe584f` gives only origin/claude/form-cli-direct-guided-01ya6p. at_unix_ms values 1790831077935, 1790832493923, 1790839622336 and 1790841638463 each read main=0 walk=1. `command grep -a -c local_generated_ids receipts/native-turn-ledger.jsonl` on main gives 0. answers.text: sr-turn-rows reads this checkout's receipts/native-turn-ledger.jsonl plus the walk checkout's, whose path comes from docs/launchd/earth.hati.day-turn.plist WorkingDirectory. The walk ledger is skipped when it is the cwd or absent. Rows are deduped by at_unix_ms+gap+option (the first checkout wins), merged in time order, and each is tagged 'checkout'. The review states the counts per checkout. Lane .out files are read from the row's own checkout. The hw-carry network retry half is deferred (host-walk.bml).
In hw-carry's fast-forward (host-walk.bml:56-58) add a live-repair for 'Could not resolve host' and 'unable to access': host_sleep_ms 60000, then hw-follow, at most twice.

title: The lane's repeat detector cannot see a repeated check failure once the candidate's bytes change: the counterexample keeps the document hash
problem: The lane's repeat detector cannot see a repeated check failure once the candidate's bytes change: the counterexample keeps the document hash
needs: In fcap-counterexample, when the retained stdout begins with 'Failed caller assertion: ', parse the JSON after ' actual=' and return [check row, exit, stdout, stderr] without document_catalog. The identities stay in checked_documents, which the verification already carries. Make this one change with F5 in the same file.
evidence: form-cli-code-policy.bml:513-514 says verification hashes 'are not the counterexample. A changed file can still produce the same failure.' But fcap-counterexample (:515-525) keeps the verification's stdout, and fcaq-check-row (form-cli-code-request.bml:88-89) writes 'Failed caller assertion: ... actual=' with the actual's document_catalog (bytes and resident_sha256) inside that stdout. Notes 6, 7 and 8 fail on the same rg row with the same actual stdout but carry shas 345d25db, 12fcb071 and cf247900. So fcap-repeat (:529) fired only at attempt 9, which had the same bytes as 8, and that is where the route turned to plan. Attempt 7's 'next: implement' was accepted over an identical failure.

answers.text: The one hook in form-cli-code-policy.bml is an import line plus one call site. fcap-counterexample now passes the stdout through fctg-assertion-core, which removes the document_catalog from a failed caller assertion's actual result. title: The FOURTH-ARM ONLY lane throws away fkwu's exit status, so a run that stops after printing its verdict reads green
problem:

A stop message such as 'fkwu: div: …' does not match the diagnostic pattern 'unresolved-call\|error:\|compiled with errors'. The lane also never reads the band's fourth-arm-bands.txt row (only the head pin), and it runs the band without the core.fk root the other lanes give it. 34 swept .fk bands declare FOURTH-ARM ONLY and are judged this way. run_fkwu_lane (line 494) and run_siblings (line 403) both check rc; this lane is the only one that does not.
The claim it breaks: validate.sh:365-366: 'A nonzero exit or source diagnostic is a failed fourth witness even when the last printed scalar happens to match (verdict-parity numbness).' validate.sh:208-210: 'Loud pass/fail — a wrong home-arm answer is a real failure'.

Write stdout, stderr and `$?` to files in a private mktemp dir instead of piping through tail, and fail with 'exit N' when rc != 0. Also read the manifest row through fourth_band_stem/awk, like run_fkwu_lane:490-497, and fail when the last line differs from it. About 12 lines. Land in sequence with G1.
evidence:
Probe band /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ursmuff-source-coherence-kernel--claude-worktrees-epic-edison-534e30/39d16a37-d4e8-4631-9ac0-105916d511fd/scratchpad/wf1/gates/stop-after-verdict.fk contains `; Verdict 7`, `; PROOF LEVEL: FOURTH-ARM ONLY (probe)`, `(do (print_str "7") (div 1 0))`.
